title: Balance of trade
competency: Calculate the balance of trade, distinguish surplus and deficit, and describe the balance of payments.

keywords.def: The value of exports minus the value of imports of goods and services in a period.
The systematic record of a nation's financial transactions with the outside world: current and capital accounts.
Exports and imports of goods and services, investment income, debt-service payments, net remittances and transfers.
Private foreign investment and public grants and loans flowing into and out of a country.
Interest payments plus repayments of principal on external debt.

en.text: The balance of trade is exports minus imports of goods and services over a period: a surplus if exports are larger, a deficit if imports are larger, balanced if equal. In 2020 Ethiopia had a trade deficit of about US$10.7 billion while China had a surplus of about US$535 billion. Some deficit is tolerable when it pays for capital equipment, but large deficits can trigger financial crises, as in Mexico (1995) and East Asia (1997–1998); trade still brings real gains.

screens.title: Are deficits bad?
paras: Some deficit is tolerable if it imports capital equipment that raises productivity and output.
Large deficits can trigger crises: foreign investors take their money out.
Real GDP can then fall 10 % or more in a single year.
Examples: Mexico 1995; Thailand, South Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia 1997–1998; Russia and Argentina around 2000.
Trade still brings gains: different endowments, economies of scale, variety of goods (Samuelson and Nordhaus, 1995).

en.text: The balance of payments is the systematic record of a nation's financial transactions with the outside world. Its current account records exports and imports of goods and services, investment income, debt-service payments and net remittances and transfers; its capital account records private foreign investment and public grants and loans. Debt service is the interest plus repayments of principal on external debt. The balance of trade is only one part of the balance of payments.

screens.title: More than goods
screens.ask: An Ethiopian working in Dubai sends money home to her family. Is this part of the balance of TRADE?
opts: No: it is a remittance, recorded in the wider balance of payments
Yes: it is an export of goods
screens.after: The balance of trade counts only exports and imports. Remittances belong to the current account of the balance of payments.

screens.title: Balance of payments
paras: The systematic record of a nation's financial transactions with the outside world.
It has a current account and a capital account.
Current account: exports and imports of goods and services, investment income, debt-service payments, net remittances and transfers.
Capital account: private foreign investment and public grants and loans flowing in and out.
Debt service: interest plus repayments of principal on external debt (Todaro and Smith, 2015).

Interest payments plus repayments of principal on external debt.

screens.text: Exports 30, imports 50, net remittances +12 (bn US$). Which is true?
opts: Trade deficit of 20; remittances cover part of it in the current account
Remittances are part of the trade balance

screens.why: Trade balance = 30 − 50 = −20. Remittances are not trade, but they are in the current account, offsetting 12 of the 20.
